newsitem.title: USA: Wachovia to buy Florida bank for $222 million.
newsitem.headline: Wachovia to buy Florida bank for $222 million.

text.p: Wachovia Corp. said Thursday it reached a definitive agreement to acquire 1st United Bancorp, a Boca Raton, Fla., commercial bank, in a stock swap valued at $222 million.

Wachovia said the agreement has been approved by the boards of both companies, but is still subject to approval of 1st United's shareholders and by regulators. It expects the merger to close by year-end.
Wachovia, which has dual headquarters in Winston-Salem, N.C., and Atlanta, Ga., is currently the 20th-largest U.S. banking company. It has assets totalling $48.5 billion.

Wachovia said the agreement provides for a tax-free exchange of Wachovia common shares for 1st United common valued at $20.875 a share of 1st United. The exchange ratio will be a minimum of 0.3 and a maximum of 0.366 of a Wachovia common share.

As part of the transaction, Wachovia said it plans to buy back up to 3.5 million of its outstanding shares. Wachovia said 1st United has granted it a stock option for about 19.9 percent of outstanding shares and directors of 1st United, who as a group hold more than 20 percent of the company's common stock, have agreed to vote in favour of the transaction.
The merger is expected to be nondilutive to Wachovia's earnings in 1998 and have a positive impact on earnings in 1999, it said.
